text: Any implementation of a function eat with this signature is acceptable, and the docstring may be changed or dropped.
The arguments may be any numbers, including non-integers.
The rabbit eats as many carrots as it can, up to what it needs (it never declines carrots it needs while some are available).
This count is narrative only and is not tied to any argument.
Carrots eaten in total, not only toward today's meals.
need is the total number of carrots for the day's meals, of which number are already eaten, so need - number are still to be eaten.
The carrots left in stock that the rabbit can still eat.
Contradiction with R-EAT-2: if remaining is the stock available, the rabbit cannot complete the day's meals when remaining is less than need, yet the prompt says it eats to complete them.
Any integer; no bound is placed on number at all.
need is at least 0; a need of 0 is a valid call.
Contradiction with R-DEF-3: if remaining is the stock available, the meals cannot be completed when remaining is less than need, yet this says the rabbit eats to complete them.
eat returns a list [total carrots eaten after the meal, carrots left after the meal], that is [number + min(need, remaining), max(remaining - need, 0)].
